title: Lord-Captain Tyragol
type: NPC · Silver Star leader and keeper of history
dek: A guarded observer who welcomes Magnus home, asks hard questions in council, cares for Aria’s funeral and gives his faction’s nomination to Wren.

facts.Role: NPC · named leader of the Silver Star
facts.Public work: Historical memory · council deliberation · faction nomination
facts.Open record: Early life, full authority and later fate unresolved

body:
Tyragol is the Silver Star’s named Lord-Captain, a public presence who keeps his own history guarded. His scenes combine quiet influence with concrete duties: welcoming a returned son, questioning plans for war, requesting funeral care and deciding whose conduct should represent the order.

The welcome before the questions

At the Niriin gathering in the Month of Moirah, Year 2, Tyragol welcomes Magnus as a lost son finding his way home. He raises a glass to the young lord’s future and says his mother would be proud of an honorable gathering.

The warmth matters beside his reserve. He is not only a title presiding over institutions; he knows how public recognition can bring a person back into a community. His praise belongs to that occasion and does not settle every later accusation against Magnus.

The observer who will not become the story

Eldin tries to draw out Tyragol’s life and stories. Tyragol hopes songs will wait until his work is done, calls himself an unobserved observer and refuses to make his own identity the subject of the conversation.

He also deflects the Lord-Captain title, saying people simply seem to like him. That modest or evasive answer does not erase the role named in the Silver Star’s public description. Nor does his comparison to a fly establish literal shapeshifting, a concealed species or an unseen office.

He does offer contacts in the Silver Star and Emerald Veil when a case interests him. Reserve can coexist with institutional reach; the exchange does not show every proposed introduction completed.

Evidence before a journey into war

At the war council Tyragol asks where a transport spell is supposed to take them when the destination is unknown. He also turns directly to Aria about a destroyed Gate. Familiarity and status do not prevent him from asking for an explanation.

When a claimed feat sounds almost too good to be true, he asks for an object that could serve as evidence. When another speaker doubts an interpretation of an attack, he asks why. He wants the reasoning brought into the room rather than left inside a reassuring conclusion.

These interventions establish a participant in collective deliberation. They do not make his every suspicion correct or give him final authority over the council’s decisions.

A history keeper asks for the body

After Aria’s death, Tyragol stands with Tarwen, whom the scene calls his good friend. Both acknowledge Draygar sadly. The men’s institutional work has a personal grief within it.

Tyragol interrupts the account to ask whether the company has Aria’s body and whether it can be returned for funeral rites. Where other speakers press responsibility and punishment, he names an immediate duty to the dead.

The request does not independently confirm the body’s location or complete its transfer.

Past, future and the choice of Wren

At the leadership gathering, Draygar puts Tyragol forward and offers himself as an adventurer ambassador. Tyragol acknowledges the respect for duty. That endorsement does not by itself appoint either man.

Tyragol speaks of knowing Zarathis’s past and of a duty to build on it while correcting mistakes. Later, as the faction nominations are given, he names Lady Wren for the Silver Star. Both interventions remain in the record: his statement of what he could bring if chosen is followed by a nomination given to someone else.

He tells Draygar that nominating himself would have been dishonorable and that Wren most closely embodies their honor and respect. Her speech makes him proud. These are his reasons for the faction’s choice, not a declaration that she wins the final contest.

His early life, complete career, the full limits of his office and later fate remain unresolved.
